text:
Step-1 :  Which of the two carbonyl compounds can exist in an enol (tautomeric) form?  
•  Cyclohexane-1,3,5-trione possesses three α-hydrogens.  Enolisation of all three carbonyl groups gives benzene-1,3,5-triol, an aromatic system.  The gained aromatic stabilisation makes the keto ⇌ enol equilibrium appreciable; hence cyclohexane-1,3,5-trione certainly shows keto–enol tautomerism.  
•  1,4-Benzoquinone has no α-hydrogen on either carbonyl carbon (each carbonyl is flanked by sp² carbons of C=C bonds).  Conversion into the corresponding “hydroquinone” would require a two-electron reduction, not a simple proton shift; ordinary keto-enol tautomerism is impossible.  Therefore benzoquinone does not show tautomerism.

Thus the compound that does NOT show tautomerism is benzoquinone.

Step-2 :  Which of the esters can show optical isomerism?  
•  Methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate, CH₃–CH(OH)–COOCH₃, contains a carbon (the second carbon) attached to four different groups (H, CH₃, OH, and COOCH₃).  Hence it is chiral and exists as a pair of enantiomers → it shows optical isomerism.  
•  Dimethyl fumarate is trans- OMeO₂C–CH=CH–CO₂Me.  Because the two ends of the double bond bear identical ester groups, the molecule possesses a centre of symmetry; it is therefore achiral and cannot show optical isomerism.

So, A = benzoquinone (no tautomerism) and B = methyl 2-hydroxypropanoate (optical isomerism).

Answer: B
